title: fmt coarse propagation taints output produced by String()/Error() methods of string-kind arguments
claim: formatArgumentKey uses any string-kind or byte-kind argument's backing identity as a coarse input even when fmt prints the value's String/Error/Format result instead of its bytes; an allowlisting Stringer yields a fully tainted (marks 0) query with no request data, collected as unsafe by the SQL sink.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -count=1 -run 'TestReview' -v ./internal/taint/propagation/ (with zz_review_coarse_test.go copied into internal/taint/propagation/ of a private copy)

title: fmt coarse propagation taints results for verbs that do not render the argument (%T, %.0s, %p, skipped %[n])
claim: Every inspected string/byte argument contributes regardless of the consuming verb, so outputs containing none of its bytes are tainted.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -count=1 -run 'TestReview' -v ./internal/taint/propagation/ (with zz_review_coarse_test.go copied into internal/taint/propagation/ of a private copy)

title: README advertises fmt.Sprint* without the direct-string/[]byte-operand restriction
claim: Tainted data inside []string, structs, pointers, and error values (errors.New(tainted)) is printed but not propagated; README lists fmt.Sprint* as supported without restriction.
repro_command: GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.6 go test -count=1 -run 'TestReview' -v ./internal/taint/propagation/ (with zz_review_coarse_test.go copied into internal/taint/propagation/ of a private copy)

title: Coarse source is the first contributor, not one lacking the surviving secure marks
claim: Marks are intersected but SourceID is the first contributor, so an unsafe coarse range can be attributed to a sanitized source while the unsanitized one is dropped; latent because no production code sets marks today.

title: Coarse owner slots consumed by snapshot entries with no ranges
claim: A clean-window entry allocates one of 4 coarseOwner slots before it is known to contribute, which can crowd out a later contributing owner.

title: Inconsistent range limit between the coarse publishers
claim: coarseStringHit/coarseBytesHit use ranges.DefaultLimit while publishCoarseOwners uses the entry limit; no behavioral effect with one range.
